title: P-A1 contrarian diagnosis + reply bait
body:
Parent: P-A0 (track A baseline)
Change: replace balanced observation with a second-person accusation + named failure mode, ending on a reusable put-down.
Why: 2026 ranking weights replies far above likes; a post someone wants to argue with out-earns a post they agree with.
Prediction: wins 3/3 on reply pull and hook, risks losing 'defensible' (the 40 tools / 9,000 tokens figures are illustrative, not measured).
Controls: same track, same budget, same judges, no media.
If it fails: the failure is about this insult's register, not about contrarian framing generally.

Candidate text:
Nobody's agent is failing because the model is too dumb. It's failing because you handed it 40 tools, 9,000 tokens of instructions, and no way to tell which ones matter. It's a skill issue and the skill is yours.

title: P-A2 subtractive insight, no fabricated metrics
body:
Parent: P-A0
Change: invert the advice (delete rather than add), keep every claim non-numeric so nothing is fabricated.
Why: tests whether rubric criterion 2 (concrete) can be satisfied without a number, since inventing a metric is forbidden.
Prediction: strong on defensible and voice, weakest of track A on concreteness.
Controls: as above.
If it fails: it rules out no-number concreteness at this length, not the subtractive angle.

Candidate text:
The fastest way to make an agent smarter is still deleting things. Tools it never calls. Instructions it can't follow. Context it doesn't read. Everyone is busy picking a model; the wins are sitting in the menu.

title: P-A3 industry tension, punchline reframe
body:
Parent: P-A0
Change: name the whole industry, compress agents to three parts, land on a reframe punchline ('the moat is the 40 rewrites').
Why: in-group recognition plus a claim about moats is the shape that gets quote-tweeted by people who half-disagree.
Prediction: highest identity score in track A, medium reply pull.
Controls: as above.
If it fails: it does not rule out industry-tension framing, only this punchline.

Candidate text:
Every AI company is shipping agents and every agent is the same three parts: a loop, a tool list, and a prompt someone rewrote 40 times at 2am. The moat was never the architecture. It's the 40 rewrites.

title: P-A4 then/now format break, aphorism
body:
Parent: P-A0
Change: abandon prose entirely for a two-line then/now structure at half the length.
Why: shortest posts have the lowest friction, and the format is instantly legible on a scrolling timeline.
Prediction: best hook, worst concreteness; a coin flip on whether judges reward brevity or read it as thin.
Controls: as above.
If it fails: it rules out this joke, not the short-format lane.

Candidate text:
2023: prompt engineering isn't a real job
2026: your company's entire output quality is one markdown file that nobody is allowed to edit

title: P-B1 mechanism first, explainer
body:
Parent: P-B0 (track B baseline)
Change: lead with the byte-level mechanism instead of with 'we built'.
Why: 'we built X' is announcement-shaped and the announcement is the least interesting part; the IEND fact is the surprise.
Prediction: wins on hook and payoff, similar identity to parent.
Controls: same budget, no link in body, no media required.
If it fails: it indicts the explainer register, not mechanism-first ordering.

Candidate text:
A PNG stops decoding at its IEND marker. Anything you append after it is invisible to every image viewer and perfectly readable to everything else.

So we ship Claude Code skills as pictures now. The image is the demo, the tail bytes are the skill.

title: P-B2 self-demonstrating: the attached image is the artifact
body:
Parent: P-B0
Change: make the post self-demonstrating - the attached image IS the skill being described.
Why: the artifact proves itself in-timeline; there is nothing to take on faith and nothing to click, which is exactly what the 2026 ranking rewards (native media, no outbound link).
Prediction: highest overall; main risk is disbelief ('X re-encodes images'), which is itself reply fuel.
Controls: same budget; media allowance is in the charter so this is not overspending.
If it fails: it would rule out this phrasing, not self-demonstration.

Candidate text:
The image attached to this tweet is a working Claude Code skill.

Not a screenshot of one. The file. Append SKILL.md after the JPEG's end-of-image marker and it rides along: renders fine, extracts in 4 lines, installs in one.

title: P-B3 trust/supply-chain angle, honest framing
body:
Parent: P-B0
Change: reframe from product announcement to a trust observation, with an explicit 'nothing is hidden' correction and a caution.
Why: the loudest reply on any post like this is 'this is a malware vector'; pre-answering it converts that reply from a dunk into a thread.
Prediction: highest reply pull in track B, lower identity.
Controls: as above.
If it fails: it does not rule out addressing the security objection, only leading with it.

Candidate text:
An image can carry an agent skill. Append a SKILL.md after a PNG's end marker: renders normally in every viewer, extracts in four lines, installs in one.

Nothing is hidden, the bytes are right there in the file. Read what you install anyway.

title: P-B4 1994 cartridge nostalgia
body:
Parent: P-B0
Change: swap the technical frame for a 1994 cartridge analogy, keeping the mechanism in the second half.
Why: nostalgia is a cheap, reliable way to make an infrastructure trick feel like a story worth resharing.
Prediction: good identity, weaker hook than P-B2 because the payoff is deferred.
Controls: as above.
If it fails: it indicts this analogy, not analogy-led framing.

Shipping Claude Code skills the way games shipped in 1994: one file, no installer, the art on the box is part of the product.

It's a JPEG. The skill is appended after the end-of-image marker. Save the picture, extract the tail, drop it in ~/.claude/skills.

title: Generic thought-leader cadence is the single biggest score sink
body: The track A default draft ('the bottleneck isn't the model, it's context') scored 3.67/8 mean and lost 8/9 pairings. Judges named the same faults each time: no hook, em-dash marketing cadence, nothing to argue with. Scoped to this draft, but all three judges converged on the same diagnosis independently.

title: Brevity beat concreteness in track A
body: P-A4 (136 chars, no mechanism, rubric 7.67) got the highest likes ratio in its track, above two 8/8 posts. Scoped: at this length and on this rubric, a legible format beat an extra checkable fact. Does not show concreteness is worthless - P-A4 still carries a specific claim in its punchline.

title: Self-demonstration is the strongest track B lever
body: P-B2 ('the image attached to this tweet is a working skill') took the highest ratio in track B; two of three judges named it the best post overall. Scoped to posts where the artifact can actually be attached - it is a claim about proof-in-timeline, not about phrasing.

title: Pre-answering the security objection helps but must not lead
body: P-B3 beat its parent 3/3 but by the smallest margin in the track, and J1 said the reassurance dampens the post. Scoped: the 'read what you install' beat is worth keeping as a closer, not as a frame.

title: Ceiling effect: every candidate swept a weak parent
body: All 8 experiments scored 1.00 preference share and 5 of 8 hit the rubric ceiling (8/8). The metric separated candidates from the default draft and nothing else - it cannot say which candidate to ship, which is the actual deliverable. Evidence: X-0001..X-0008.

Applies to: references/roles.md builder brief; enforced at wave 2 candidate authoring.

paraphrase (P-A4p) as the noise probe. Borda points: rank 1 = 13, rank 14 = 0.

| P-A1 (w1 survivor) | 8.67 | [10, 1, 5] | 1/3 |
| H4 (hybrid B2 x B4) | 7.67 | [2, 10, 7] | 0/3 |

| P-A4p (noise probe (paraphrase of P-A4)) | 3.67 | [12, 13, 6] | 0/3 |
| P-B0 (anchor) | 1.33 | [13, 12, 13] | 0/3 |
| P-A0 (anchor) | 0.00 | [14, 14, 14] | 0/3 |

Noise probe: P-A4 ranked [3,2,3]; its paraphrase P-A4p ranked [12,13,6]. The judges are consistent
with each other (spread 1 and 7 respectively) but violently sensitive to wording - a reworded
version of a top-3 post fell ~8 places. Read that as: rank differences of 1-2 places mean nothing,
and phrasing is a bigger lever than topic.

Per-post judge spread is the reliability signal. Tight: P-A4 [3,2,3], H3 [4,3,2], H6 [9,9,9].
Loose (judge-dependent, do not trust the mean): P-B2 [1,7,4], H2 [8,6,1], P-A1 [10,1,5], P-A3 [6,4,12].

Verdict by experiment:
- H3 (self-demo x mechanism-first): only post in the top four for all three judges, and the only
  post all three said they would repost. QUALIFIED.
- H2 (then/now x 2am detail): rank 1 for J3, rank 8 for J1. Judge-dependent, no separation from its
  parents. INCONCLUSIVE.
- H1, H4, H5, H6: all placed below at least one parent. REJECTED. J3, unprompted: "mashups lose to
  their parents; blending two hooks dilutes both."
- Anchors P-A0 (14,14,14) and P-B0 (13,12,13) came last, as they should if the judges have any taste
  at all. This is the only within-campaign check on the strawman-baseline confound (I-0005) and it is
  a weak one: it shows the anchors are bad, not that the winners are good.

Status: evidence_ready

note: H1 ranked [7,11,10], below both parents. Stacking the accusation into the then/now format made it a three-line post and cost the format its only advantage: speed.
H2 ranked [8,6,1]. J3 called it the best post in the pool, J1 put it eighth. No separation from its parents; inconclusive, not a win.
H3 ranked [4,3,2], the only post inside the top four for every judge and the only unanimous would-repost. Beats its parent P-B2 [1,7,4] on consistency, not on mean.
H4 ranked [2,10,7], below parent P-B2 for two of three judges. Two hooks competing in 258 chars.
H5 ranked [5,5,11]. The security closer did not carry its weight inside the self-demo frame; B-0004 stands but does not generalise to this stack.
H6 ranked [9,9,9] - unanimously mid. Answers I-0002: the then/now FORMAT is not a transferable lever; it worked for P-A4 because of what that post says, not because of its shape.

title: H3c factual correction: PNG/IEND -> JPEG/FFD9
body:
Parent: X-0011 (H3)
Change: PNG/IEND replaced with JPEG/FFD9, because the file that must be attached for the post's
first sentence to be TRUE is a JFIF - X re-encodes PNG uploads and that destroys the appended tail.
This is a defect found in pre-flight, not a style edit: the qualified winner made a claim its own
artifact could not keep.
Prediction: no engagement regression; the point is truth, not score.
Controls: same 3 judges, blind, randomized position, single pair, same budget.
Result: 2 of 3 judges preferred the corrected version (1.25x, 1.15x); J1 preferred the original at
1.3x on the grounds that IEND is more legible than FFD9. Judges split on which version carried the
factual risk, and one of them (J1) had the direction backwards: it is PNG uploads that X re-encodes.
Truth decides this one, not the vote - and the vote did not contradict it.

Final text:
The image attached to this tweet is a working Claude Code skill.

A JPEG stops decoding at its FFD9 end marker. Everything after it is invisible to every viewer and perfectly readable to everything else. That's where the SKILL.md is. Save it, read the tail.

title: The qualified winner made a claim its own artifact could not keep
body: H3 told readers to save a PNG and read its tail, but a PNG uploaded to X is re-encoded and the tail is destroyed. Six blind judges across two waves scored it without noticing; it was caught by reading the repo README against the post. Generalisation: LLM judges score plausibility, not whether the artifact behaves as described.

title: Pre-flight check: every factual claim re-read against the artifact, not the judges
body: Evidence-worker brief gains a final gate before any result is called shippable: re-read each claim in the winning text against the actual artifact and the platform it will be posted on, and record the check. Judges are a proxy for taste only; they are not a proxy for truth. Applies to references/roles.md, evidence worker brief.

title: Combining two qualified hooks reliably lost
body: Four of the five hybrids (H1, H4, H5, H6) ranked below at least one parent, and J3 wrote the same conclusion unprompted. Scoped to hooks: these posts each carry one attention-grabbing move, and two of them in 250 chars split the reader's attention. Says nothing about combining a hook with a supporting detail, which is what H3 does and H3 won.

title: The then/now format is not a transferable lever
body: H6 put the cartridge content into P-A4's winning format and landed unanimously mid-pool [9,9,9]. Scoped: the format did not carry a different payload. P-A4 wins on what it says.

title: Phrasing dominates topic at this length
body: A trivial-looking paraphrase of a top-3 post fell ~8 ranks with all three judges agreeing. Scoped to 140-char posts: word choice is a bigger lever than any structural change tested in this campaign.

title: LLM judges score plausibility, not truth
body: Six judge runs scored a post telling people to save a PNG from X and read its tail. None flagged it. When finally asked directly about factual risk, two judges disagreed with each other and one had the re-encoding direction backwards. Scoped: use judges for taste, verify claims against the artifact.

note: Not promoted: ranks [8,6,1] are judge-dependent and never separate it from P-A4 or P-A3. Rejected as 'no evidence of gain', not as 'worse' - worth retrying only with a different judge panel.
